inline.s: Question: How can one attain assurance of rebirth?
Answer: To have assurance of rebirth is to have assurance of fulfilling the conditions for rebirth. The condition for rebirth is:
ten thoughts in unbroken succession at the time of death.

This condition for rebirth was taught by Master Shandao (a reincarnation of Amitābha Buddha), Master Yongming (a reincarnation of Amitābha Buddha), and the enlightened masters Tanluan and Daochuo; it is the valid testimony of the sage. (For details, see
The Conditions for Rebirth
) Therefore, to attain assurance of rebirth is:
ten thoughts in unbroken succession, accumulated practice becoming second nature.
To this end, Master Shandao taught:
“It is precisely because reciting the Name is easy
(precisely because reciting the Buddha's name is easier than contemplating the Buddha)
, that unbroken recitation brings birth
(unbroken mindfulness of the Buddha at the time of death brings rebirth)
. If one can keep the thoughts unbroken, right up to the end of life, then ten out of ten will be reborn, a hundred out of a hundred will be reborn.
May all people reflect well upon this: whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down, you must spur and restrain yourselves
(urge yourselves on and discipline yourselves)
, never letting up day or night
(never cease the unbroken succession of thoughts, day or night)
. When the previous thought ends your life, the very next thought brings rebirth. To enjoy forever the bliss of the unconditioned Dharma, and at last to attain Buddhahood — is this not delightful!”
(For the annotation, see
Master Shandao's Pure Land Teachings
) The twelfth patriarch of the Pure Land school, Master Chewu, also taught:

“Therefore we should recite this one name of Amitābha a thousand times, ten thousand times, reciting all day and all year, for no other purpose than to make this single thought thoroughly familiar. If this one thought becomes truly matured, then at the time of death there will be only this one thought and no other.”
On Buddha-Recitation (Annotated Record of Master Chewu's Teachings): The Final Thought at Death

[Valid testimony of the sage] This is spoken by the sage, correct and without error, and can be received with full confidence. [Unbroken succession of thoughts] The thoughts of Buddha-recitation link together, uninterrupted by deluded thoughts. [Accumulated practice becoming second nature] Through repeated practice, making it instinctive.
